title: Monsoon Reverie
story: Painted over three wet-on-wet sessions during last year's monsoon, this canvas chases the exact grey-gold light that falls over the Western Ghats just before the rain breaks. Layers of thinned acrylic were poured and tilted rather than brushed, so the pigment settled the way water finds its own path down a hillside.

title: Still Life with Marigolds
story: A kitchen-table study of marigolds left over from a Ganesh Chaturthi puja, painted before the petals dried. The palette knife work in the shadows was an attempt to keep the flowers a little unruly, the way they actually sat in the jar.

images.alt: Still Life with Marigolds, full view of the oil painting
Still Life with Marigolds, close-up of the impasto petals

title: Threshold I
story: The first in an ongoing series about doorways and the pause before crossing one. Plaster, marble dust and pigment are built up in bands and then partially sanded back, so the panel reads differently depending on how close you stand.

title: Coastal Drift
story: Made from memory a week after a trip to Gokarna, this piece is less a record of the coastline than of how tired, salt-heavy eyes remember it: flattened bands of colour, no horizon line to anchor them.

Coastal Drift, shown installed on a gallery wall

title: Interior, Evening Light
story: A small study of a hallway in the studio at the one hour of the day when the light turns amber. Painted quickly, in a single sitting, before it changed.

title: Terracotta Skies
story: A square canvas built from the same red-earth pigments used in the ceramic work, ground finer and bound in acrylic medium. It is the closest the painting practice comes to the sculpture practice.

story: This composition — thread and paper pulp worked into the canvas ground — is offered as a commission concept rather than a finished stock piece, so scale, palette and materials can be adapted to your wall.

title: Kinship
story: Two welded forms lean into each other without quite touching. Cast bronze elements are inlaid into raw steel and left to oxidise naturally, so the surface will keep shifting colour for a few years after it leaves the studio.

title: Vessel of Memory
story: Hand-built using a coiling technique rather than thrown on a wheel, so the walls stay slightly uneven on purpose. A single firing, ash-glazed.

title: Standing Figure No. 3
story: Third in a series of elongated standing figures built from a single block of terracotta rather than cast. The surface is worked with a cold patina after firing to slow down how quickly the eye reads the form.

title: Reliquary
story: The largest freestanding piece made in the studio to date. Sheet steel is cut, folded and welded into a hollow reliquary form, then left outdoors for six weeks to oxidise unevenly before a wax seal locks the finish in place. Because of its size and weight this piece ships by specialist freight — request a quote below and we'll arrange crating and door-to-door delivery.
